judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the master image of the Contact us page: a reproduction of Michael Rothenstein's print 'Rush' (1975), an airmail envelope stamped URGENT over an airliner with 'Rush' written twice, marked alt="" inside a figure. Its visible figcaption, which is exposed to assistive technology, names the artist, the title 'Rush' (linked to the artwork's page on Tate's site), the date and the copyright, so the claim that the surrounding text does not say 'Rush' is false, and the model had this caption in its ancestor context. The 'URGENT!' stamp is a painted detail of the artwork, not information the contact page conveys. In context the picture is a thematic illustration, and the content needed to use the page is all in the text. A decorative image with null alt, identified by a caption, meets 1.1.1 (H67). Some auditors might still want a short alt describing the artwork, but the finding's claim, that words in the image carry information missing from the page, does not hold up. The live page on 2026-10-23 has the same markup.
